 Judgment
The Insurer-respondent No.2 in ECA No.4/2017 on the file of learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner for Compensation at Athani, (for short, "the Commissioner")
, is impugning the judgment and award dated 29.02.2020 awarding compensation of Rs.8,88,880/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
2. Parties are referred to as per their rank before the Commissioner for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, the claimants are the parents and brothers of deceased Anand Irappa Kumbhar, have filed the claim petition under Section 3 read with Section 28 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, claiming compensation for the death caused in the accident.
It is submitted that, on 02.03.2010, the deceased was driving the tractor and trailers bearing Registration Nos.KA.23/TA-804, 805 and 806 was transporting the sugarcane to the sugarcane factory.

When he reached near the land belonging to Prakashgouda Patil on Mudhol-Jamkhandi road at 6 a.m., he lost control over the vehicle and as a result, the tractor and trailers turtled and the driver died.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 24 years, working as a driver and earning handsome amount.
The claimants were depending on him and therefore they have claimed compensation.
Respondent No.1 being the Insured and respondent No.3 being Insurer of the tractor and trailers were arrayed as parties.

Even though respondent No.2 was initially arrayed as party,
subsequently its name is deleted.
4.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the Tribunal and filed his statement of objections denying the contention taken by the claimants.
However, it is contended that as on the date of accident, the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 and therefore, it is respondent No.3 who is liable to pay the compensation.

5. Respondent No.3 filed statement of objections denying the contention taken by the claimants,
while admitting the fact that the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
It is contended that the deceased was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and therefore it is not liable to pay compensation.
6. On the basis of these pleadings, the following issues came to be framed.

"1. Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased by name Anand Kumbar was engaged by the respondent No.1 as driver of tractor and trailer bearing Reg.
No.KA-23/TA-804, KA-23/TA-805 and KA-23/TA-806 6 respectively on 02.03.2010 at about 06:00 a.m., near the land of Prakashgouda Patil within the limits of Mallapur village on Mudhol-Jamkhandi road, due to the rash and negligent manner,
the tractor and trailer caused the accident, as a result the deceased sustained grievous Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Shri. Irappa S/O. Rayappa Kumbhar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12994552/
3 injuries all over the body and succumbed at the spot?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

7. The claimant examined as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 9.
Respondent No.3 got examined DW.1 and got marked documents Exs.R.1 to R.16 in support of its contention.

8. The Tribunal taking into consideration all these materials on record came to the conclusion that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,88,880/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of petition till realization from respondent Nos.1 & 3 jointly and severally.
9. Being aggrieved by the same, respondent No.3 is before this Court.

10. Heard Sri Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Prasad R. Siddhanti,
learned counsel for respondents-claimants.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the driver of the tractor and trailer was not having driving licence to drive the same.
The charge sheet was filed against the deceased under Section 3 of the Workmen's Compensation Act for not having the driving licence to drive the vehicle in question.
Respondent No.3 issued the notice as per Exs.R.3, 12 and 15 to the claimant and insured calling upon them to produce the driving licence of the deceased.
The postal receipts and postal acknowledgements were also produced.
Inspite of that neither the claimants nor the insured have produced the driving licence of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, it is a clear case of driving the offending vehicle without any driving licence and therefore the insurer is to be exonerated from paying the compensation.
Accordingly prays for allowing the appeal.
12. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 4 fairly concedes that the deceased was not having driving licence to drive the vehicle in question.
However, he would contend that it is a social legislation that the claim against respondent No.3 is to be allowed.
13. Perused the material on record.

The point that would arise for my consideration is as under:
"Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Commissioner calls for any interference by this Court?"
14.

My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS 15.
The only point raised by learned counsel for the appellant is that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

4 produced Ex.P.8, the charge sheet filed against the deceased Anand Kumbhar for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC and under Section 3 of Workmen's Compensation Act read with 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that the deceased was the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence to drive the same.
16. Respondent No.3 led evidence of RW.1 in support of its defence.
Ex.R.2 is the copy of the insurance policy, Ex.R.3 is the notice under Order 11 Rule 16 calling upon the claimant to produce the driving licence of the deceased.
Exs.R.4 to 7 are the postal receipts and Exs.R.8 to 11 are postal acknowledgements for having served the notice on them.
Ex.R.12 is the copy of the notice issued to the insured calling upon him to produce the copy of the driving licence.
Postal receipts and postal acknowledgements are produced as per Exs.R.13 and 14.
A notice was also issued to the respondent No.5-Regional Transport Officer, Chikkodi, Belagavi District as per Ex.R.15, calling upon him to produce the driving licence of the deceased.
Ex.P.16 is the postal receipt.

These documents disclose that the deceased was charge sheeted for the offence under Section 3 of the Workmen's Compensation Act read with Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act for not having driving licence while driving the tractor and trailer in question.
Even though respondent No.3 issued the notice to respondents-claimants, insured and also to the Transport Authority, none of them have produced the driving licence pertaining to the deceased.
The same would support the contention of respondent No.3 that the deceased was driving the vehicle in question without driving licence.
Under such circumstances, there is violation of the terms and conditions of policy, which goes to the root of the matter and therefore the insurer is to be exonerated from paying the compensation.
17. I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Commissioner.
The Commissioner has not taken into consideration these aspects of the matter and mechanically proceeded to award compensation saddling liability on the Insurer.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Commissioner is liable to be set aside.

18. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
a) The appeal is allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award dated  29.02.2020 in E.C.A. No.4/2017 by Additional  Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner for  Compensation, Athani is hereby set aside.
- 10 -  Consequently, the claim petition against the  appellant-Insurer is dismissed.

c) Draw award accordingly.
